findings.summary: schedulerStatus reports STALLED whenever lastTickAt is older than 60s while the scheduler pid is alive. The scheduler only starts a tick when the host is stale AND work is queued, so an idle healthy scheduler is shown as STALLED. Make STALLED depend on a live tick record older than the limit, or queued>0 with a stale lastTickAt.

findings.summary: The recorded tick pid is checked only with kill(pid, 0); after pid reuse an unrelated process could be signalled once the age passes the limit. Consider also checking the scheduler liveness or process start time.

findings.summary: The watchdog signals -pid then pid from a recorded tick pid; after a scheduler crash a stale record plus pid reuse could signal an unrelated same-user process. Store the scheduler pid or process start time and only reap when it matches, or signal only the negative pid.

findings.summary: `pid` is a const read by the onExit callback; a synchronous onExit would hit the temporal dead zone. Latent only; declare `let pid` before the call.

findings.summary: Watchdog and status share hostStallMs but read different env sources (deps.env vs process.env); benign. A legitimately slow tick would be killed at 60 s; AI_SDLC_TICK_STALL_MINUTES is the documented escape.

findings.summary: Round-1 pid-reuse finding is fixed (only process.kill(-pid) now). Remaining risk needs a scheduler crash, pid reuse and a group leader at once. Optional hardening: store the scheduler pid in the tick record and reap only on match; isAlive checks the single pid rather than the group.
